classification: authored game content; fictional people, no real individuals
note: The character cast: rival CEOs, central bank chairs, state governors and party leaders. Roles are what a person can be asked to do; the engine fills posts from this list, preferring people whose scenario matches. Stance runs from -100 (dovish) to +100 (hawkish) and is present only for chair-capable people. Portraits are drawn by tools/cast_portraits.py.

people.name: Walter Pruitt
people.background: Ran a small drilling contractor for 30 years and bought distressed leases whenever prices fell. He is blunt, distrusts banks, and is happiest taking a rival's rigs at auction.

people.name: Marisol Ybarra
people.background: Chemical engineer from Rice who rose to run refining at a Houston major. She ties wells, pipelines and refineries into one chain and favours steady credit over tight money.

people.name: Desmond Broussard
people.background: Former Louisiana state treasurer who now runs a pipeline and petrochemical lender. He knows which Gulf operators are over-borrowed and prices loans accordingly.

people.name: Helen Kowalczyk
people.background: Daughter of a steelworker, she became chief financial officer and then chief executive of a Cleveland steel maker. She keeps large cash reserves and wants slow, predictable growth.

people.name: Kenji Watanabe-Moore
people.background: Runs an auto-parts supplier his mother's family started, and has opened three new plants in a decade. He prefers adding capacity to buying competitors.

people.name: Gloria Abernathy
people.background: Spent 25 years as an economist at a regional reserve bank, then ran a Chicago commercial lender. She argues that tight money hurts factory towns first.

people.name: Priya Raman
people.background: Chip designer who moved into management and now runs a firm making both processors and the boards around them. She likes owning every step from design to shipping.

people.name: Joel Brandvold
people.background: Venture investor who made money early in cable and software, and lost some of it in a 1987 crash. He backs fast growth and cheap credit, and trades his own stakes often.

people.name: Linh Tran
people.background: Software founder who sold her first company at 27 and put the money into three new ones. She chases unproven markets and changes direction quickly.

people.name: Ingrid Vossberg
people.background: Economist who worked 20 years at the national central bank before joining a Rhine chemicals firm's board. She holds that price stability comes before everything else.

people.name: Emre Kaplan
people.background: Son of a Turkish steelworker, he built a river freight and scrap business and now buys troubled Ruhr suppliers cheaply. Established firms in the region still treat him as an outsider.

people.name: Tobias Wendt
people.background: Mining engineer who became head of a coal and steel group and spent the 1980s converting old pits into industrial parks. He wants the region retrained and rebuilt, not sold off.
